extraction_metadata.notes: Extraction from the Nature Scientific Reports open-access article. Effect sizes are approximate ranges drawn from the published abstract and figures; precise values require full-text verification.

title: Hesperetin reduces neuronal death in an SH-SY5Y model of oxidative stress via NF-κB inhibition
subtitle_or_tagline: A citrus flavonoid with documented Caspase-3 pathway modulation and an established TCM safety record.
topic: Hesperetin (a citrus flavonoid) protects differentiated SH-SY5Y neurons from H2O2-induced oxidative stress by reducing NF-κB activation, lowering intracellular ROS, and modulating downstream apoptotic markers including Caspase-3.

components.name: Oxidative-stress model
components.role: H2O2 challenge on differentiated SH-SY5Y neurons to induce apoptotic cascade.

components.name: Hesperetin treatment
components.role: Dose-response pre/post incubation with the flavonoid.

components.name: Mechanistic readouts
components.role: MTT viability, LDH release, intracellular ROS (DCFH-DA), NF-κB luciferase, western blot for Caspase-3 / Bax / Bcl-2.

architecture.data_flow: SH-SY5Y differentiation → H2O2 insult ± Hesperetin → viability / ROS / NF-κB / apoptotic-marker panel → mechanistic interpretation.
output_types: Caspase-3 / Bax / Bcl-2 protein expression (western blot)

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Differentiate SH-SY5Y cells (retinoic acid protocol).
Step 2 - Apply H2O2 insult to model oxidative stress.
Step 3 - Treat with Hesperetin at graded doses.
Step 4 - Read out viability (MTT), cytotoxicity (LDH), ROS (DCFH-DA).
Step 5 - Quantify NF-κB activity and apoptotic markers (Caspase-3, Bax, Bcl-2).
Step 6 - Establish mechanistic chain: ROS → NF-κB → Caspase-3 → apoptosis.
key_claims: Hesperetin pre-treatment significantly rescued SH-SY5Y viability under H2O2 insult.
Intracellular ROS was reduced by Hesperetin in a dose-dependent manner.
NF-κB luciferase activity was attenuated, consistent with anti-inflammatory mechanism.
Caspase-3 and Bax protein levels were lowered; Bcl-2 was raised — consistent with apoptosis suppression.
The mechanism places Hesperetin upstream of Caspase-3, distinct from direct active-site inhibition.
caveats_or_warnings: Effect sizes are approximate; precise values require full-text verification.
Hesperetin's mechanism is upstream (ROS / NF-κB) rather than direct Caspase-3 active-site binding — distinct from Magnoflorine's docking-predicted direct inhibition.
SH-SY5Y is a cell line, not primary tissue; in vivo validation required.
Bioavailability of dietary flavonoids is poor; formulation strategy required for therapeutic use.

molecule_metadata.name: Hesperetin
molecule_metadata.source: Citrus fruits (oranges, lemons, grapefruit); aglycone of hesperidin.
molecule_metadata.notable: Planar flavonoid scaffold — better BBB permeability than the aporphine alkaloid Magnoflorine. BBB predictor should score this higher.
molecule_metadata.tradition: Dietary intake; TCM uses citrus peel (chenpi) rich in hesperetin glycosides.
